# SuperGrep

> Retrieval + inference offload for AI coding agents. Four tools over an
> Infino index kept in two places: `find` and plain `sql` run on your
> machine over the keyword index; `search`, a `sql` statement with a ranked
> search inside it, and `ask` run in the Infino cloud over the same index's
> platform copy, where the embeddings are computed. `ask` hands a question
> to small models on the service that work the index and return the rows
> they found, cited `path:line`, rather than prose. The package, the CLI
> (`cx`) and the MCP server are still named `code-context`.

SuperGrep is built on infino (https://github.com/infino-ai/infino), a
retrieval engine that runs SQL, full-text (BM25) and vector search over one
copy of the data. Try it live at https://infino.ai/supergrep.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): what it is, the one-command install, what it saves,
  where it wins and where it does not, indexing from object storage.

## Using it

- Install: the Claude Code plugin, once per machine -
  `claude plugin marketplace add infino-ai/supergrep` then
  `claude plugin install code-context@infino-ai`. Any directory a session
  opens is indexed on its first question; `find`, `sql` and `read` need no
  account and upload nothing. `search` and `ask` need one: the person runs
  `npx -y @infino-ai/code-context login --platform https://api.supergrep.infino.ai` once, in a
  terminal - it asks, creates a free account (key at `~/.infino/key`, mode
  600), and every directory after that has all four tools, each in its own
  database, uploaded the first time `search` or `ask` is used in it. `cx
  install` writes a per-repository `.mcp.json` entry for other clients.
- MCP tools (stdio): `find` (every line containing an exact string, written
  like `grep -n` with per-file counts; complete and unranked), `search` (one
  ranked pass fusing exact terms with meaning; hits carry the code and their
  citation), `sql` (read-only SELECT/WITH over
  `chunks(path, start_line, end_line, lang, symbol, content)`, with
  `bm25_search`, `hybrid_search`, `vector_search` and `token_match` as
  table-valued relations so a search composes with GROUP BY), `ask` (a
  question that spans the repository, returned as the rows found). `read`
  returns the numbered lines of files the index named, several in one call.
  `find`, `search` and `sql` take `queries`, several in one call, and an
  optional `path` (absolute repository root) so one server serves several
  local repositories; `ask` is scoped to the one platform database the
  server was started with. No reindex tool: the first query builds the
  index and every query re-syncs it.
- CLI: `cx install`, `cx login`, `cx index` (incremental; `--full`,
  `--watch`, `--no-embed`, `--max-files`), `cx find`, `cx search`, `cx sql`,
  `cx status`, `cx usage`, `cx mcp`.
- Corpora that do not fit on a laptop are written out as Parquet in object
  storage and indexed there by the platform (`POST /v1/hydrate`); nothing
  passes through the machine.

## Evidence

- [What it saves](README.md#what-it-saves): the same 36 questions about a
  256,000-line codebase, with and without SuperGrep, on Claude models,
  every claim checked against the code. Cheaper on every model; more fully
  correct answers on the cheapest; level on the larger ones.
- [Where it wins, and where it does not](README.md#where-it-wins-and-where-it-does-not):
  by kind of question.
- [Embedder eval](docs/embedder-eval.md): how the local embedding model
  behind `--embed-provider local` was chosen.

## Operational notes

- The local index lives in `.infino/` in the directory root (added to
  `.gitignore` on the first build): plain files you can copy or cache in CI.
  With an account the same chunks also load into a platform database over
  HTTPS, authenticated by a bearer key that is never passed as a
  command-line argument.
- Keyword search is live within seconds of the first build; the platform's
  vectors backfill behind it and semantic ranking unlocks when they land.
- Incremental sync re-chunks and re-embeds only changed files (size/mtime
  prefilter, then content hash); an unchanged tree is a fast no-op, and
  every sync updates both copies.
- Config via env: `CX_ROOT`, `CX_INDEX_DIR`, `CX_AUTO_INDEX`, `CX_AUTO_SYNC`,
  `CX_SYNC_INTERVAL_SECS`, `CX_NO_EMBED`, `CX_MAX_FILES`,
  `CX_MAX_FILE_BYTES`, `CX_TABLE`, `CX_TEXT_COLUMN`. Platform settings are
  command-line flags on `cx index` and `cx mcp`; see
  [the reference](docs/reference.md).
